evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry says 打 is absent from the main Shuowen and appears in its later “Newly Attached” section, where it is analyzed as 从手、丁聲 (“from hand, 丁 as phonetic”) and glossed “strike.” It records 都挺切 as the older reading and cites later 丁雅切/modern dǎ, as well as the English-derived dozen counter dá. This supports 扌 as semantic and 丁 as phonetic; it does not establish any earlier graphic ancestor or corruption.
evidence.title: [A01498] 打 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database analyzes 打 as from 手 with 丁 phonetic and identifies striking/collision as its basic sense. It cites Han-period 王延壽’s 賦 poem use “撞縱目，打三顱,” and later examples for attack and fighting in 梁書, making early lexical use potentially earlier than the Shuowen New Attached entry. It reports no oracle-bone or bronze examples in its form table; one small-seal form is listed. The citations do not establish an uninterrupted semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「打」

evidence.source: 徐時儀, 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微
evidence.field: earliest attestation and disputed textual history
evidence.text: The paper states that present Shuowen lacks 打 and that it appears in the Song-era 徐鉉 New Attached section. It discusses claims of earlier occurrences in Han and Tang materials, including citations in 玄應’s Buddhist lexicon and an alleged Shuowen quotation, but notes uncertainty about whether these reflect an earlier Shuowen text or later transmission. It reports an early definition in 通俗文 as “撞出曰打” (roughly, an object knocked/struck out is called 打). Thus the claim that Shuowen is the earliest extant use is not secure; earlier textual evidence exists but its transmission and exact dating need caution.
evidence.title: 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database separately cites Han 王延壽 for a striking use, 梁書·侯景傳 for attacking, 梁 任昉 for beating/fighting, Song 歐陽修 for making or manufacturing, and Tang 李德裕 for a prepositional use marking place/direction/time. These are dated textual examples, not proof that each sense directly developed from the preceding one.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「打」

evidence.source: 徐時儀, 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微
evidence.text: The article considers whether forms historically written with 木 and later 手 could be related to 打, reviewing arguments that an older graph may have been confused or replaced. It concludes that the proposed identity between earlier 本/木 forms and 打 is not established by the extant pre-Song dictionaries and rhyme books: form, sound, or meaning differ in the records. This is a disputed proposal, not evidence for a proven corruption pathway.
evidence.title: 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微

evidence.field: 丁 and 打 historical phonology
evidence.text: For the 丁 phonetic series it lists Zhengzhang Old Chinese 丁 *rteːŋ, *teːŋ and 打 *rteŋʔ, *teːŋʔ. The shared onset/rime and nasal support a phonetic relationship, while the departing suffix/entering tone distinction reflected in reconstructions leaves details of the precise historical relation reconstruction-dependent. These are reconstructions, not direct recordings of ancient pronunciation.
evidence.title: 打 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The listed series includes 丁 *rteːŋ, *teːŋ alongside 打 *rteŋʔ, *teːŋʔ and multiple other 丁-series forms. This supports the phonetic role of 丁 independently of uncertainty over the earliest depicted referent or shape of 丁; no claim about a pictured tool or weapon is needed for the component analysis.
evidence.title: 打 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database reports Guangyun entries 德冷 and 都挺 and classifies them in Middle Chinese categories as 端母梗攝上聲, respectively 庚/梗 division II and 青/迥 division IV. These are separate rhyme-book readings; the source does not by itself explain their semantic or dialectal distribution.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「打」

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong article by 徐時儀; cited in search result and examined PDF
evidence.text: The article surveys competing proposals for the later open-rime reading: analogy with 搭/搨, influence from 撻, or regional loss of the nasal coda. It cites Song-period rhyme-book evidence for 都瓦切/都假切 and Yuan 中原音韻 placement in 家麻. These accounts dispute a single certain path from the older nasal reading to modern dǎ; the timeline is about pronunciation, not graphic development.
evidence.title: 「打」的形、音、義衍變遞壇探微

evidence.source: Kangxi Dictionary entry reproduced at zdic.net
evidence.field: historical pronunciations and early lexical citations
evidence.text: The entry reports 都挺切 and cites the Shuowen analysis; it also records 六書故 都假切, 韻會/正韻 都瓦切, Tangyun 德冷切 and 歐陽修《歸田錄》滴耿切. It cites 谷梁傳 commentary for 捶打, but this is a later annotation of an ancient passage and does not establish that 打 itself occurred in the original transmitted passage.
evidence.title: 打 dǎ、dá - 汉典

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes modern Mandarin dǎ for extended senses of the striking verb from dá, a dozen as a transliteration of English dozen. It provides dated examples for ‘strike’ from Tang 杜甫, for later ‘take/catch fish’ from Song 汪元量, and many later extensions including ‘attack’, ‘make’, ‘buy’, ‘remove’, ‘print’, and ‘from/since’. A dictionary’s ordered list is not evidence for the order or direct semantic derivation of these extensions.
evidence.title: [A01498] 打 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The entry treats the dozen sense as a separate word history, associating 打 with the transliteration 打臣 from English dozen. The Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary independently identifies 打 as an English-dozen transliteration used for a unit of twelve. This is a whole-graph use for a different word/sense, not evidence about 丁’s phonetic role in the striking graph.
evidence.title: 打 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The entry compares the striking word with Mizo dêng ‘throw, fling, hammer’ and Proto-Mon-Khmer *dah ~ daʔ ‘hit, meet’, with Mon and Khmer forms. These are proposals, not established cognates or a demonstrated loan direction. No inspected primary comparative source independently verified the forms, sound correspondences, early attestations, or borrowing direction here; the comparison should remain tentative.
evidence.title: 打 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

gaps: No actual oracle-bone or bronze attestation was found in the consulted character databases; absence from those listings does not prove the character did not exist earlier.

The asserted earliest Han occurrence in 王延壽 and the early 通俗文 citation are mediated by later textual witnesses. The scholarly discussion explicitly questions whether alleged early Shuowen material reflects an original Shuowen text; dates and transmission require manuscript-level verification.
No glyph images were visually inspected. The databases list one small-seal form, but this research does not establish a sequence of dated graphic transformations or a specific corruption event.

The idea that 打 replaced or derives graphically from a 木-form remains disputed; inspected evidence does not establish an ancestor-descendant relation. No component origin_form classification beyond modern 手/扌 and 丁 is warranted from these sources.

The semantic relationship between striking, attacking, making, collecting, multiple light-verb uses, and the prepositional sense is not demonstrated as a complete chronological chain. Dictionary sense order was not treated as chronology.

The historical comparison of 打 with Mizo dêng and Proto-Mon-Khmer *dah/*daʔ could not be independently validated from primary comparative sources. Sound correspondences, source-word chronology, direction of borrowing, and whether these are cognates, loans, or chance similarities remain unresolved.

Although 丁’s phonetic role is supported by the Shuowen New Attached analysis and the cited Zhengzhang series, reconstructions differ by system and stage. The component’s own original referent is unnecessary to this phonetic claim and was not independently established.
The separate dozen sense is associated with English dozen, but the inspected sources do not supply a dated first attestation for the Chinese counter use or the intermediate form 打臣.
